memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. Diploma (DPLM-GB) is a first-rank 'Compounder' whose shares at 7,105p (£71.05, 2026-09-15) have already been paid for the year that will not repeat: on the record's modal path the total shareholder return is about 11.3 percent a year over eighteen months and 10.1 percent a year over three years, a D against the framework's 20 percent bar. The park rule is not triggered by any gate item (management A; business quality B; predictability A; trackability C); the case is parked on its return, with a downside to F on a plausibly worse drop-through from EBITDA to earnings per share. Progress the case on either of two triggers: a price of about 5,500p or lower on unchanged earnings (about 6,350p on the eighteen-month test), or evidence at the 17 November 2026 results and the January 2027 update that FY2027 guidance sits above the long-term model (organic growth of 8 percent or better; a margin of 26 percent or better), which would move the bull branch from possible to probable and the 'Investment Thesis' to a C. Conviction is medium because the arithmetic is robust and the branch odds are judgement.
case: The thesis: Diploma is a first-rank 'Compounder' whose shares have already been paid for the year that will not repeat; at 7,105p and 25.5x earnings 24 months forward, the next stage (mid-single-digit earnings growth in FY2027 as Peerless's supernormal margin is given back by choice, then 10 to 11 percent a year from the acquisition engine) returns about 10 to 11 percent a year against the 20 percent bar; the 20 percent case reappears at about 5,500p or on evidence by January 2027 that FY2027 is not the deceleration year the company itself describes.

The change was real, broad and is now mature. Since 2019 the company doubled through about £1.6bn of acquisitions at 8x EBIT, moved about half of revenue into structurally growing niches (aerospace, defence, data centres, nuclear, water) and lifted the adjusted margin from the high teens to a guided 26.5 percent. In eighteen months the change travelled the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain: resources (chief executive since 2019; chief financial officer confirmed December 2025), choices (the pivot; a 4,000-target pipeline; the model held at 5 percent organic and 10 percent total), actions (15 deals for £310m; CDM), operating metrics (organic growth 14, 15, 15 percent by quarter; 10 percent outside Peerless), financial statements (operating profit up a little over 40 percent; earnings per share up about 45 percent from £1.75 to £2.54), sell-side estimates (consensus FY2026 up 37 percent in twelve months; eleven of eleven raising; three guidance raises). The share price travelled with it (5,030p to 7,105p, +41.3 percent over six months) and has stopped: minus 0.4 percent over three months while the July upgrade added 7 percent to FY2026 consensus.

External forces (B): demand structural in the half of revenue in aerospace (order books 10 to 12 years; short-term growth capped by supply, not demand), defence (3 to about 7 percent of revenue pro forma for CDM and Spring Solutions; a Czech facility), data centres (Windy City Wire to $40m in three years; a single-digit share of group revenue); the other half flat to down (International Seals minus 1 percent organic in H1 FY2026 with "early signs of stabilisation" at Q3; Life Sciences +4 percent; Canadian public healthcare "highly challenging"). Competition easing relative to broadline peers (RS Group at 0 percent organic and a 9.2 percent margin; Rexel and Fastenal six quarters of organic declines). Tariffs a relative advantage (75 to 85 percent of US products sourced locally against Grainger's 20 percent and RS Group's 34 percent from China). Headwinds: the company's own cycle at a peak year (FY2026 abnormal, 15 percent not to repeat, Peerless to settle at high-single-digit growth; the base beneath is 5.7 percent organic over fifteen years, 7 percent over seven, above target in 15 of 20 years); the supply side, because the aerospace fastener tightness that took Peerless's margins from 35 percent at acquisition to above 50 percent is easing and management is managing spot prices down (a structurally higher floor of 35 to 40 percent expected; spot about 30 percent of Peerless volume); sterling translation (over 80 percent of revenue outside the UK; H1 FY2026 minus £17.9m revenue and minus £7.6m operating profit; about 9.33p of earnings per share per 10 percent USD/GBP move); European stagnation.
counter_case: At Building Block 1, the sell-side majority's "better for longer" (Rothschild & Co Redburn), in its strongest form: Diploma has permanently shifted its margin profile and growth algorithm; the business outside Peerless grows at 10 percent on structural demand with years to run (aerospace backlogs of 10 to 12 years; defence 7 percent of revenue and rising; hyperscaler commitments secured); Peerless's contract conversion lifts its baseline margin so that the "normalisation" is to 40 to 45 percent, not 35, because aerospace supply tightness persists for years; £600m of capacity deployed at 8x is 10 to 14 percent accretive to earnings per share within a year; the 26 percent margin therefore holds; FY2027 earnings per share grow 12 to 15 percent, not 4; the multiple holds at 25 to 26x because Halma sits at 24.6x with less growth, the Swedish serial acquirers at 26 to 27x with less quality, and the market pays for safe havens; the return is 20 to 25 percent a year and the case is a B. The evidence for it is real: the Q3 update beat every broker on the organic line, growth outside Peerless accelerated to 10 percent, the 26.5 percent margin guidance "shattered even the most bullish estimates", the record of guiding low is twenty years long, and two of the eleven brokers already carry FY2028 earnings per share of £3.03 and £3.11 against a median of £2.74. The record concedes the quality, the record, the capacity; that the bull branch is a genuine 30 percent, not a tail; that a held multiple gives a C, not a D; that its 24x and 23x are judgements, not measurements; and that it makes no bounded-downside claim, because no division covers the enterprise value at any multiple in the comparison set (Controls' divisional operating profit of about £369m for FY2026, on consensus segment revenue of £1,101m at the H1 33.5 percent margin, is a pre-tax divisional figure; against an enterprise value of £9,893m it is 26.8x, and at the sector's lowest multiples of about 9x it covers about a third), so the downside is bounded by the multiple's floor and nothing else. The record holds because the company is the witness against the bull case: it says FY2026 is abnormal, that 15 percent will not repeat, that 26.5 percent is the top end of sustainable, that Peerless is being priced down and will settle at high-single-digit growth, that returns will settle at 15 to 20 percent as deployment accelerates, and it refuses to raise a 5 percent organic model; the median consensus already carries the margin give-back; the price stalled for three months while the last upgrade landed; the bull branch needs two correlated conditions to hold at once through the toughest comparatives in the company's history (a Peerless margin at or above 45 percent, possible at about 40 percent; organic growth outside Peerless at or above 8 percent, plausible at about 55 percent; joint about 30 percent); and even the bull earnings path with a drifting multiple is a C, so only bull earnings with a held multiple is a B, a cell put at about a quarter.

At Building Block 2, the risks digest's false-friend profile: the positive signals mask an underlying deceleration and a structural decay in aerospace pricing; Day-1 inclusion of acquisitions in organic growth adds about 200 basis points (true organic growth 4 percent, not 6); systems spend starved to flatter margins (cash software and capital expenditure £1.3m in H1 FY2026); working capital deteriorated (£58.9m outflow; receivables up £35.5m); the adjusted margin 510 basis points above statutory; pay escalated. The record concedes the adjusted-to-statutory gap, the Day-1 choice (Morgan Stanley's rebuttal: 10 to 50 basis points long-run), the working-capital build and the pay optics, and holds because the disconfirming evidence the digest itself named has appeared: growth outside Peerless 10 percent, not 4, on the company's own Q3 disclosure; Seals and Life Sciences grew; cash conversion 105 percent in FY2025 with the H1 dip seasonal; capital expenditure £7.6m in the half on the financials block's basis, not £1.3m; the margin expansion volume-led with Peerless worth about 100 basis points. The digest's own verdict is that the bear thesis being materially correct is of low plausibility. Where it is right: the earnings-quality mark and the monitoring burden (receivables ageing; capital expenditure; the spot-to-contract ratio).
triggers: - Progress triggers: a price of about 5,500p or lower on unchanged earnings (about 6,350p on the eighteen-month test; about 5,000p on the drop-through path); or FY2027 guidance at the 17 November 2026 results and the January 2027 update above the long-term model (organic growth 8 percent or better; margin 26 percent or better), which would move the bull branch from possible to probable and the 'Investment Thesis' to a C. What would change the view on the Peerless path: a January 2027 update with Controls organic growth at or above 12 percent and FY2027 margin guidance at or above 26 percent.

- The Peerless margin path ('Case/SP Key Driver'): current margin above 50 percent, growth above 40 percent, spot about 30 percent of volume; modal 38 to 42 percent by H2 FY2027; guidance "taper" and high-single-digit growth; consensus group margin 24.9 percent FY2027; Alarm level: group margin guidance below 25 percent; Invalidate level: Peerless margin below 40 percent with growth below high-single digits within two quarters.

- The acquisition engine ('Case/SP Key Driver'): £310m in twelve months at 8x, £600m capacity at 0.8x; modal £300m a year at 8x; guidance £200m to £300m a year, returns 15 to 20 percent over three years; consensus none unannounced; Alarm level: nothing deployed over six months; Invalidate level: a deal above 12x EBIT, or leverage above 1.5x without accretion. What would change the view: two quarters without a deal, or a deal above 12x, or leverage above 1.5x without accretion.
- Earnings growth on the path ('Case/SP Key Driver'): Alarm level: FY2027 earnings per share flat on FY2026 at about £2.55, the drop-through path on which the return is an F.
- The multiple ('Case/SP Key Risk'): 25.55x; modal 24.0x at eighteen months and 23.0x at three years; no Alarm level (a price signal, not a series); the entry level about 5,500p.

- A value-destructive large deal ('Case/SP Key Risk'): CDM at 11x and 17 to 18 percent margins; modal toward 20 percent within eighteen months and no deal above 12x; Alarm level: no progress on CDM's margin at the FY2027 results; Invalidate level: a write-down; a deal above 12x.
